module_title: Subordinate Courts - Appointments and Tribunals (Part XIV-A)
introduction: At this level, we look at the specific qualifications required to become a District Judge and dive into the constitutional provisions for Tribunals, which were added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.

core_concepts.title: Appointment of District Judges (Article 233)
core_concepts.description: Qualifications required: 1. Should not already be in the service of the Central or State Government. 2. Must have been an advocate or a pleader for at least 7 years. 3. Should be recommended by the High Court for appointment.

core_concepts.title: Appointment of other Judicial Officers (Article 234)
core_concepts.description: Appointments to the judicial service of a state (other than District Judges, like Civil Judges) are made by the Governor after consulting the State Public Service Commission (SPSC) and the High Court.

core_concepts.title: Administrative Tribunals (Article 323A)
core_concepts.description: Added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) under Part XIV-A. It empowers the Parliament to set up Administrative Tribunals (like CAT) to resolve disputes related to the recruitment and service conditions of public servants.

core_concepts.title: Tribunals for Other Matters (Article 323B)
core_concepts.description: It empowers both the Parliament and State Legislatures to establish tribunals for other specific matters like taxation, foreign exchange, land reforms, and labor disputes.

important_entities.name: Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)
important_entities.significance: It provides speedy and inexpensive justice to central government employees regarding their service disputes. It is guided by the principles of 'natural justice' rather than strict civil procedure codes.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Tribunals under 323A can be established ONLY by the Parliament. However, tribunals under 323B can be established by BOTH Parliament and State Legislatures (depending on their legislative competence).

A Sessions Judge has the power to award any punishment, including the death penalty. However, a death sentence passed by them is NOT valid until it is confirmed by the High Court, irrespective of whether an appeal is made or not.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: A for Administration, B for Broad/Basics
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: 323A is strictly for Administrative service matters. 323B is a Broad category covering all other basic matters (taxes, land, etc.).

exam_strategy_tips: The '7 years as an advocate' requirement for becoming a District Judge is a highly repetitive question in State PCS and SSC exams.
